root_causes.evidence: Network p95 is 2010 ms against a 29 ms baseline, with a 6.8% error rate. Clearing logs show repeated network timeouts on item 97, and the clearing queue has built up to 145 items.

escalation.reason: Clearing is healthy; item 97 waits because the external network times out (p95 2010 ms, 6.8% errors), so this is an external outage that needs escalation, not a quarantine.; Every internal component is at baseline, but the network has worsened from slow to fully down: 100% of calls fail and the clearing backlog is 535 and growing. I am escalating again so the owner knows it is now a full outage.
escalation.ask: The national payment network, as seen from our clearing worker, has p95 latency of about 2 s (baseline 29 ms) and about 7% timeouts. Clearing queue depth is 145 and growing. Please contact the network operator to restore service. Payments are posted to the ledger and are waiting to clear; nothing on our side needs changing.; UPDATE: the national payment network is now fully down, not just slow. 100% of clearing's calls time out at about 2 s. The clearing backlog is 535 posted payments and growing, with the oldest waiting about 62 s. Please contact the network operator urgently and declare an outage to customers if needed. Our systems are healthy and need no change. Payments are accepted and posted correctly, and the ledger is balanced. Clearing will drain the queue automatically when the network recovers. Do not quarantine queued items: they are valid and are only waiting on the network.

sbar.situation: Recovery is not confirmed: the external national payment network is fully down, and payments are failing at the clearing step. The clearing backlog is 762 items and growing, with the oldest waiting 87 s and nothing being processed.
sbar.background: The network's p95 latency rose to 2010 ms against a 29 ms baseline, with a 6.8% error rate, and then went to 100% failed calls. Clearing logs show repeated network timeouts on item 97, which has waited 87 s after 39 attempts.
sbar.assessment: The root cause is an external outage of the network (confidence 0.85), and no allowed action can fix it. The incident commander escalated to the network operator twice, the second time to say it is fully down, and took no other action because no internal component needs one.
sbar.recommendation: Follow up with the network operator, decide with them whether to declare an outage to customers, and expect the recovery check to keep failing at clearing until they restore service. Do not quarantine queued items, because they are valid and clearing will drain them when the network returns. Operations should review the 762 delayed payments, which are posted to a balanced ledger but not yet cleared.
